title: Simple Past: Regular and Irregular Verbs / Haɗin Wuro: Verbooji Rewɓe e Maɓɓe
bridge: Nden ineespañol, haɗin wuro naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo (fui, comí, viví). Ingiilisi, verbooji rewɓe naaɗoɗo -ed (talk → talked), amma verbeoji maɓɓe naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo (go → went). Ko ɗum wuro ingiilisi naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo (I went, you went, he went), ko ineespañol naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo (fui, fuiste, fue). Jariɗo faaɗum 'did' aɗaɗaɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo!
rule: Haɗin wuro ingiilisi naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo. Verbooji rewɓe, naaɗoɗo -ed (work → worked, play → played). Ko verbooji naaɗoɗo e 'e', naaɗoɗo -d (live → lived); ko naaɗoɗo e consonante + 'y', 'y' naaɗoɗo 'i' e naaɗoɗo -ed (study → studied). Verbooji maɓɓe naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo (see → saw, eat → ate) ko naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo. Aɗaɗaɗo 'did' + forma base e verbooji (I didn't go, Did you see?). Forma afirmativa naaɗoɗo 'did'. Haɗin wuro naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo 'yesterday', 'last week', 'in 2010'.

concept_examples.text: I walked to the park yesterday.
She ate an apple for breakfast.
We didn't watch TV last night.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ˈdɪdnt wɑːtʃ tiː ˈviː læst naɪt/

common_error.correct_alt: She didn't go to school yesterday.
common_error.explanation: Dum wuro ineespañol naaɗoɗo e verbooji maɓɓe (fue), amma ingiilisi, aɗaɗaɗo 'did' (auxiliar e haɗin wuro), verbooji maɓɓe naaɗoɗo e forma base: 'go'. Jariɗo: 'did' naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo, ko verbooji maɓɓe naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.

examples.original: I played football last Sunday.
examples.translation: Miɗo yahɗeɗo futa eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: Naaɗoɗo -ed e verbo 'play' eɗɗoɗo 'played'.

examples.original: She studied for the exam.
examples.translation: O yahɗeɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: Ko verbooji naaɗoɗo e consonante + 'y', 'y' naaɗoɗo 'i' e naaɗoɗo -ed: study → studied.

examples.original: We lived in Madrid for two years.
examples.phonetic: /wiː lɪvd ɪn məˈdrɪd fər tuː jɪrz/
examples.translation: Enen yahɗeɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: Verbo 'live' naaɗoɗo e 'e', ko naaɗoɗo -d: lived.

examples.original: I went to the cinema with my friends.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ went tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə wɪð maɪ frendz/
examples.translation: Miɗo yahɗeɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: 'Go' maɓɓe: 'went' e haɗin wuro. Jariɗo eɗɗoɗo maɓɓe eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo go-went, see-saw, eat-ate.

examples.original: She saw a beautiful bird in the tree.
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː sɔː ə ˈbjuːtɪfl bɜːrd ɪn ðə triː/
examples.translation: O yiite maayoɗum eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: 'See' naaɗoɗo 'saw'. Maaɓɓe 'seed'.

examples.original: He ate all the cookies.
examples.translation: Ko yiite maayoɗum eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: 'Eat' naaɗoɗo 'ate'. Yimɗe eɗɗoɗo /eɪt/, maaɓɓe /iːt/.

examples.original: I didn't like the movie.
examples.translation: Mi yiite maayoɗum eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: Aɗaɗaɗo 'didn't' + verbooji e forma base. Verbo 'like' naaɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.

examples.original: Did you finish your homework?
examples.translation: Nden yiite maayoɗum eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo?
examples.note: Aɗaɗaɗo 'Did' + sujeto + verbooji base. 'Did' naaɗoɗo e afirmativas.

examples.original: They didn't come to the party.
examples.translation: Be yiite maayoɗum eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo eɗɗoɗo.
examples.note: Jariɗo: 'come' maɓɓe, amma aɗaɗaɗo negación naaɗoɗo e forma base 'come', maaɓɓe 'came'.

title: Presente Continuo
bridge: En inglés, el presente continuo (am/is/are + verbo -ing) se usa para acciones que están ocurriendo ahora mismo o en un periodo temporal actual. En pulaar, usamos el presente simple para ambas cosas (''estoy hablando'' vs ''yo hablo''). La trampa principal es que los hispanohablantes suelen olvidar el verbo auxiliar ''to be'' o confunden cuándo usar el presente simple frente al continuo. A diferencia del pulaar, el inglés distingue claramente entre una acción habitual (present simple) y una acción en progreso (present continuous).
rule: El presente continuo se forma con el verbo ''to be'' conjugado (am, is, are) + el verbo principal con terminación -ing. Se usa para: 1) acciones que están ocurriendo en el momento de hablar (''I am reading now''), 2) acciones temporales que suceden alrededor de ahora (''She is working in Madrid these days''), y 3) planes futuros (''We are meeting at 5''). No se usa con verbos de estado (like, want, know, prefer) excepto en casos especiales. La forma negativa añade ''not'' después del auxiliar (''I am not sleeping''), y la interrogativa invierte el auxiliar (''Are you listening?''). En pulaar, el presente progresivo (estar + gerundio) es similar, pero el inglés lo usa más a menudo que el pulaar, especialmente para acciones temporales.

concept_examples.translation: O yahii e jangu e Madrid.

common_error.explanation: Este error ocurre porque en pulaar no se añade una terminación especial al verbo cuando se usa el progresivo (''mi yahii'' vs ''mi anndi yahii''). En inglés, después del auxiliar ''to be'' siempre va el verbo con -ing. Para evitarlo, recuerda la estructura: sujeto + am/is/are + verbo-ing. No olvides la terminación -ing.

examples.original: I am eating.
examples.translation: Mi anndi naange.
examples.note: Usa 'am' con 'I'.

examples.original: He is running.
examples.translation: O anndi yahii.
examples.note: Usa 'is' con he, she, it.

examples.original: They are playing football.
examples.translation: Be anndi yahii fute.
examples.note: Usa 'are' con you, we, they.

examples.original: We are watching TV.
examples.translation: En anndi yiite la teeveesiyo.
examples.note: Recuerda cambiar 'y' a 'i' y añadir -ing (watch > watching).

examples.original: I am not sleeping.
examples.translation: Mi anndi maayii.
examples.note: La negación se forma con 'am not', 'is not', 'are not'.

examples.original: She is not crying.
examples.translation: O anndi maayii.
examples.note: Contracción común: isn't.

examples.original: Are you studying?
examples.translation: A anndi naange?
examples.note: Invierte el sujeto y el auxiliar para preguntar.

examples.original: What is he doing?
examples.translation: A anndi yahii?
examples.note: Las preguntas wh- llevan el auxiliar después de la palabra interrogativa.

examples.original: He is working in London these days.
examples.phonetic: /hiː ɪz ˈwɜːkɪŋ ɪn ˈlʌndən ðiːz deɪz/
examples.translation: O anndi yahii e London teemaaji.
examples.note: Se usa para acciones temporales, no habituales.

examples.original: We are going to the cinema tomorrow.
examples.phonetic: /wiː ɑːr ˈɡəʊɪŋ tə ðə ˈsɪnəmə təˈmɒrəʊ/
examples.translation: En anndi yahii naange sinema.
examples.note: Se usa para planes futuros.

examples.original: I like this song.
examples.translation: Mi joodo fii ndiyam nden.
examples.note: No digas 'I am liking' porque 'like' es un verbo de estado.

examples.original: She doesn't want to go.
examples.translation: O maayii yahii.
examples.note: Usa el presente simple con verbos de estado como want, know, prefer.

title: Futuro con going to / Future with 'going to'
bridge: En pular, puɗɗe eɗɗe futuure eɗɗitiiɗe eɗɗe ndaɗaama eɗɗe ndaɗaama eɗɗe ndaɗaama eɗɗe ndaɗaama eɗɗe. En inglise, la estructura 'be going to + verbe' eɗɗe laaɗaama eɗɗe 'ir a + infinitivo' eɗɗe, ɗaɗaama eɗɗe ndaɗaama eɗɗe ndaɗaama eɗɗe. En inglise, to be conjugué (am/is/are) ɗaɗaama eɗɗe 'going to', ɗaɗaama eɗɗe ndaɗaama eɗɗe ndaɗaama. Aammu, 'going to' eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe
rule: Fuɗɗe eɗɗe 'going to' eɗɗe: suɓɓe + verbe 'to be' (am/is/are) + 'going to' + verbe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe. En affirmatif: 'I am going to travel' (maɓɓeɗo ndaɗaama eɗɗe). En négatif: 'I am not going to travel' (ko maɓɓeɗo ndaɗaama eɗɗe). En interrogatif: 'Are you going to travel?' (ɗaɓɓeɗo ndaɗaama eɗɗe?). Se contre souvent: 'I'm going to', 'You're going to', etc. Eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe: 1) Planes eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe (I'm going to study medicine), 2) Predicciones eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe (Look at those clouds! It's going to rain). Eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe 'will': 'I'll help you'). Aammu, 'going to' eɗɗe eɗɗe 'to be'.

concept_examples.text: I am going to visit my grandmother tomorrow.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈvɪzɪt maɪ ˈɡrændˌmʌðər təˈmɑːroʊ/

concept_examples.text: She is going to buy a new car.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə baɪ ə nuː kɑːr/

concept_examples.text: We are not going to watch TV tonight.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː ɑːr nɒt ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə wɒtʃ ˌtiːˈviː təˈnaɪt/

concept_examples.text: Are you going to come to the party?
concept_examples.phonetic: /ɑːr juː ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə kʌm tə ðə ˈpɑːrti/

common_error.wrong: I going to travel next week.
common_error.correct: I am going to travel next week.
common_error.correct_alt: I'm going to travel next week.
common_error.explanation: En pular, 'ir a' eɗɗe eɗɗe verbe auxiliar conjugé, eɗɗe inglise 'going to' eɗɗe verbe 'to be' (am/is/are) eɗɗe. Oɗɗitɗe 'am' eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe. Aammu: sans 'am/is/are', la phrase eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe.

examples.original: I am going to study English tonight.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈstʌdi ˈɪŋɡlɪʃ təˈnaɪt/
examples.translation: Miɗoɗo ndaɗaama eɗɗe eɗɗe maama maama.
examples.note: Yahɗe 'am' eɗɗe 'I'. Aammu la contre eɗɗe: 'I'm going to'.

examples.original: They are going to have dinner at a restaurant.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ ɑːr ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə hæv ˈdɪnər æt ə ˈrestrɑːnt/
examples.translation: Be eɗɗe eɗɗe maama eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe.
examples.note: Eɗɗe 'they' eɗɗe 'are'. 'Have dinner' eɗɗe 'cenar'.

examples.original: He is going to call his boss.
examples.phonetic: /hiː ɪz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə kɔːl hɪz bɒs/
examples.translation: O yahɗe eɗɗe maama eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe.
examples.note: Eɗɗe 'he/she/it' eɗɗe 'is'.

examples.original: I am not going to eat fast food.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ æm nɒt ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə iːt fæst fuːd/
examples.translation: Ko miɗoɗo ndaɗaama eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe.
examples.note: En négatif, añade 'not' eɗɗe eɗɗe verbe 'to be'.

examples.original: Is she going to travel to Spain?
examples.phonetic: /ɪz ʃiː ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə ˈtrævəl tə speɪn/
examples.translation: O yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe?
examples.note: En questions, pon le verbe 'to be' eɗɗe eɗɗe début, comme eɗɗe pular: 'ɗaɓɓeɗo o yahɗe...?' (aammu eɗɗe pular eɗɗe eɗɗe inverser).

examples.original: They aren't going to stay at home.
examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ ˈɑːrnt ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə steɪ æt hoʊm/
examples.translation: Be eɗɗe ko yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe.
examples.note: Puedes eɗɗe contre 'aren't' eɗɗe 'are not'.

examples.original: Are you going to help me?
examples.translation: Mi yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe?
examples.note: Fijate eɗɗe la différence eɗɗe pular: ici eɗɗe 'are you' eɗɗe début, eɗɗe pular eɗɗe eɗɗe 'ɗaɓɓeɗo o yahɗe...?' eɗɗe eɗɗe.

examples.original: Look at the clouds! It is going to rain.
examples.phonetic: /lʊk æt ðə klaʊdz! ɪt ɪz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə reɪn/
examples.translation: Wonaa eɗɗe eɗɗe! O yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe.
examples.note: Eɗɗe 'going to' eɗɗe predicciones eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe.

examples.original: She is going to be late (she missed the bus).
examples.phonetic: /ʃiː ɪz ˈɡoʊɪŋ tə biː leɪt (ʃiː mɪst ðə bʌs)/
examples.translation: O yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe (o yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe).
examples.note: La evidencia eɗɗe o yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe 'going to'.

examples.original: The car is going to crash!
examples.translation: O yahɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe!
examples.note: En situaciones eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe eɗɗe 'going to'.
